publisher_assessment.publisher: Normattiva and the named Italian government departments, courts, authorities, and EU discovery service.
publisher_assessment.decision: Accept the 35 distinct official source records through 37 official links within recorded scopes, and accept three reviewed Normattiva local statutory representations. No legal topic or country review is accepted or complete.
publisher_assessment.basis: Normattiva identifies itself as the Italian legal-text service and describes persistent URNs and original, current-at-consultation, date-selected, and multivigent views. The reviewed current records provide consolidated government texts for the main free-movement, immigration, administrative-procedure, and judicial-procedure acts. Current MAECI and authority pages can be human-reviewed in the official web view even where direct capture clients receive a security challenge. On 24 October 2026, complete article-level current-text captures of D.Lgs. 30/2007 (28 article records), Law 218/1995 (80), and Law 184/1983 (92) were replay-verified against official Normattiva responses. All article identifiers and order matched the live current-text pages; all extracted sections were non-empty. Comparing the previous and fresh captures found no wording changes after whitespace normalization; Law 184/1983 had one paragraph-break-only serialization change. The 2026-10-24 as-of date is the capture date; Law 184/1983 did not expose an ELI version date. The 24 October migration archived 42 candidate/inventory artifacts and 205 capture artifacts (203 Normattiva raw responses plus two retrieval manifests) in the Monitor local-only archive. The duplicate pack-local Normattiva capture-manifest alias had the same SHA-256 as the retrieval manifest and was removed after comparison; only one canonical archive record remains.
publisher_assessment.limitation: External-link acceptance means that the named official page is a usable reference within its exact role, wording, language and date. It does not accept a local conversion, establish full topic coverage, resolve every legal dependency, or complete Italy review. Several links are dated, discovery-only, operational examples or live pages without a publication date.

material_dependencies.instrument: Decree-Law 24 February 2026, No. 23, converted by Law 24 April 2026, No. 54
material_dependencies.material_effect: The coordinated Normattiva text records the amendment to D.Lgs 286/1998 Article 4(3) concerning specified criminal convictions in entry conditions. The current TUI text should be read together with this amendment where relevant.

In force from 4 June 2026; Article 1 amends D.Lgs 286/1998, including Articles 4-bis and 5, to implement Directive (EU) 2024/1233. Review the relevant current TUI provisions for any issue involving those amendments.

policy: A trustworthy official government consolidated text or clearly identified official page may be accepted as an external reference within its displayed status, version, language, date and subject. If authority, version or content is unclear, offer the whole official government website/service for human review. A human-reviewed link is sufficient for ordinary source use; a local copy, custom retrieval/conversion rule, API, full Gazette amendment chain, hash, replay or scheduled update is not a blanket prerequisite. External-link acceptance is separate from local-copy acceptance, issue/topic coverage and country review completion.
